agentic-loop: A single illustration shows a circular assembly-line loop in which an AI agent repeatedly improves its work: on one side, a model writes code; next, a small renderer displays the resulting webpage or game screen; then a magnifying eye or inspection lens examines the visual output and marks a visible error; after that, a tool-equipped hand edits the code; and the cycle returns to rendering again, with several faint repeated versions arranged around the loop like drafts. A person is present only as a distant supervisor, emphasizing long autonomous revision. Around the loop, the scaffolding, screens, connectors, and tools are drawn as prominently as the central model, showing that the surrounding harness is essential; the overall image should read as iterative drafting and checking rather than a single question-and-answer exchange.
mixture-of-experts: A single panoramic illustration depicts a massive translucent AI system as a circular amphitheater containing hundreds of small hexagonal expert chambers, with 896 of them visible but only 16 brightly lit for one incoming word or prompt; a central routing mechanism, drawn like an intelligent lantern or switchboard, sends thin beams to the selected chambers while the rest stay dark, showing that each input uses only a few experts. The lit experts pass their partial answers through connecting threads to a small output point, while beneath the amphitheater an enormous memory vault stretches down into the ground, filled with dense parameter blocks, conveying broad knowledge and huge memory requirements. To one side, a tiny ordinary computer strains beneath the full structure but cannot hold it, while a cost meter near the output reads low computation per word, making clear that mixture-of-experts models combine vast total capacity with cheap, selective activation.
model-distillation: A single illustration should show a large, luminous teacher model as a towering workshop or machine releasing a flowing stream of finished answer tokens, diagrams, and polished texts toward a smaller student model that is carefully copying and reshaping those outputs into its own form; between them, a tense border or courtroom-like dividing line suggests a dispute over permission, with one side gesturing accusingly at the other for taking the teacher’s outputs, while beneath both models a vast ocean of human-written pages, books, and public text supports the whole scene, making clear that distillation is both a normal learning method and a politically charged argument about who may learn from whose outputs.
open-weights: A single wide illustration shows two versions of the same AI model: on the left, a sealed opaque black box sits behind a corporate counter, reachable only through a narrow app or API window, its interior hidden and a large off switch hanging above it; on the right, the box opens into a vast transparent lattice of billions of numerical weights, spilling out like luminous ledgers into a warehouse of server racks, where copies are loaded onto different machines, examined with lenses, adjusted with fine-tuning tools, and carried away to other data centres, while the off switch on the left casts a shadow but cannot extinguish the distributed weights, making clear that open weights let large operators inspect, modify, preserve, and continue running a model even after its creator might try to withdraw or control it.
